quod: quī, quae, quod — which (rel., n. nom./acc. sg.); quod (conj.), because, that · also interrog. adj., what? (n. nom./acc. sg.: quod genus) · also acc. of respect, wherefore (quod tē per superōs … ōrō) · also indef. adj. after sī, any (n. nom. sg.: sī quod nūmen) · also connective, but, now (quod sī, 'but if'; n. acc. sg. as conj.)
quos: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. or interrog., m. acc. pl.) · quis after sī — any(one) (indef., m. acc. pl.: sī quos)
rauca: raucus, -a, -um — hoarse, harsh-sounding (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
regis: regō, regere, rēxī, rēctum — to rule, direct (2nd sg. pres.) · also rēx, rēgis (m.) — king (gen. sg.: regis tectis)
saltem: saltem (adv.) — at least, at any rate
satus: serō, -ere, sēvī, satum — to sow, beget; satus, sprung from (+ abl.) (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sedibus: sēdēs, sēdis (f.) — seat, abode, home; base, foundation (abl./dat. pl.)
senior: senior, -ius — older, aged; senior (m.), an elder, old man (comp. of senex, m. nom. sg.)
servat: servō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to keep, guard, preserve, watch (3rd sg. pres.)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sine: sine (prep. + abl.) — without · also sinō, -ere, sīvī, situm, to allow, let (sg. imper.: sine palmula)
sollemnia: sollemnis, -e — yearly, solemn, ritual; sollemnia (n. pl.), rites, ceremonies (n. acc./nom. pl.)
sortemque: sors, sortis (f.) — lot, fate, condition, allotted span (acc. sg.) + -que, and
sperare: spērō, -āre, spērāvī, spērātum — to hope, hope for (pres. inf.)
spes: spēs, speī (f.) — hope, expectation (nom. sg.; also acc. pl.)
spoliata: spoliō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to strip, rob, deprive (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.)
stagna: stagnum, -ī (n.) — standing water, pool; waters (acc./nom. pl.)
stant: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3rd pl. pres.)
stygia: Stygius, -a, -um — of the Styx, Stygian, infernal (f. abl./nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
sublimis: sublīmis, -e — high, aloft, on high (f. nom. sg.)
sum: sum, esse, fuī — to be (1st sg. pres.)
summa: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost; surface of (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. nom. sg. (rēs summa; summa diēs)
surgentis: surgō, -ere, surrēxī, surrēctum — to rise, spring up (pres. part., m. acc. pl., -īs for -ēs)
tacitum: tacitus, -a, -um — silent, unspoken, secret (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
tam: tam (adv.) — so, so much, to such a degree
tanta: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (ex tantā urbe)
tantis: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
terrae: terra, -ae (f.) — earth, land, country (gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
thalamo: thalamus, -ī (m.) — bedchamber, inner room, bridal chamber (abl./dat. sg., Greek)
thesea: Thēseus, -eī (m.) — Theseus, Athenian hero who entered the underworld (acc. sg., Greek form)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
traxitque: trahō, -ere, traxī, tractum — to drag, draw (3rd sg. perf.) + -que, and
trementem: tremō, -ere, tremuī — to tremble, quiver (pres. part., f. acc. sg.) · also m. acc. sg. (Priamum trementem)
tris: trēs, tria — three (m./f. acc. pl., = trēs)
tristi: tristis, -e — sad, grim, bitter, harsh (m./f./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
tristis: tristis, -e — sad, grim, gloomy (m./f. nom. sg.; acc. pl. in -is = -ēs)
troia: Trōius, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (abl. sg., from Troy) · also nom. sg., Troy (servātaque serves Trōia fidem)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tumulum: tumulus, -ī (m.) — mound, hillock, burial mound (acc. sg.)
turbidus: turbidus, -a, -um — stormy, wild, confused, turbulent (m. nom. sg.)
tuta: tūtus, -a, -um — safe, sheltered (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
ullum: ullus, -a, -um — any (n. nom./acc. sg.; also m. acc. sg.)
ultro: ultrō (adv.) — of one's own accord, voluntarily; besides
umbra: umbra, -ae (f.) — shade, shadow (abl. sg.; nom. sg.)
uncis: uncus, -a, -um — hooked, curved, crooked (m./f./n. abl. pl.)
uno: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (m./n. abl. sg.)
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
vectos: vehō, vehere, vexī, vectum — to carry; pass. to be borne, travel (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.)
vel: vel (conj., adv.) — or; even; vel… vel, either… or
venti: ventus, -ī (m.) — wind (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl., in address (sine nūmine, ventī)
venturum: veniō, venīre, vēnī, ventum — to come (fut. act. part., m. acc. sg.; with esse understood, 'would come')
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
verrunt: verrō, -ere, verrī, versum — to sweep, skim (3rd pl. pres.)
vi: vīs (f.; acc. vim, abl. vī) — force, power, violence (abl. sg.)
vides: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (2nd sg. pres.)
vincla: vinc(u)lum, -ī (n.) — chain, bond, fetter (nom./acc. pl., shortened form of vincula)
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl. (festīnāte, virī)
viribus: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, strength; pl. vīrēs, vīrium, strength (abl./dat. pl.)
viridisque: viridis, -e — green, fresh (f. acc. pl., = viridēs) + -que, and
vita: vīta, -ae (f.) — life, living; the breath of life (nom. sg.; also abl. sg.)
